Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in a non-equimolar cation–anion amorphous Li2Zr0.625Ta0.3Cl4.2O0.9 oxyhalide electrolyte derived from Li2ZrCl6, achieving 4.11 mS cm−1 conductivity and high-voltage tolerance via a self-passivating interphase. Its significance is enabling fast-charging, high-voltage all-solid-state batteries, retaining 81.2% capacity after 2,000 cycles at 10 C, advancing high-energy-density solid-state lithium batteries.

item.title: A High-Nickel Cathode Material for Lithium-Ion Batteries Integrating a Proposed 3D Ionic Percolation Network and Interwoven Layered/Rock-Salt Nanodomains
item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 High-energy neutron irradiation reconstructs single-crystal LiNi0.92Co0.06Mn0.02O2, creating a proposed 3D Li+ percolation network via grain boundaries plus interwoven layered/rock-salt nanodomains. This dual architecture shortens diffusion paths, suppresses phase transitions and side reactions, delivering 213.9 mAh/g at 0.2 C and 80.0% retention after 450 cycles at 5 C—establishing neutron irradiation as a novel cathode engineering strategy.
